cells.tense: Here, the shape gets laid cleanly and you know when to stop pushing.
cells.act: tend the small thing and learn from it
cells.ask: Pick one part of what you're building and tend it like a beginner tends a growing thing — watch what it does, and change the plan to fit what you find.
cells.core: You can set a shape and let it settle, and when something needs structure you make the first piece solid before reaching for the rest. The wait isn't lack of nerve. A plan built this way holds weight, because each piece got to sit before the next landed, and the person standing inside it can feel it was built to last rather than to hurry. Pick one part of what you're building and tend it like a beginner tends a growing thing — watch what it does, and change the plan to fit what you find. The care stays intact without being proven by speed, and what you learn goes back into how you build.
cells.sheetLine: You tend the piece that's here and learn its pace.
cells.verb: Completing and governing through the authority that knows what to release as well as push.
cells.place: Where a mess is turned into a shape someone can walk through.

cells.tense: The shape is being pushed toward a form that hasn't arrived yet.
cells.act: put the inquiry on paper and follow it
cells.ask: Write the next open question about the plan on paper, then follow only where the answer actually leads.
cells.core: When you're building something, you need the shape to be right, so you draft steps the material hasn't reached. The plan runs past the ground beneath it. And the people who will stand inside feel the tightness first, because tomorrow's piece is already decided before today's has set. Rigor built this structure, so rigor can pace it. Write the next open question about the plan on paper, then follow only where the answer actually leads. That's a small piece of the method. The building isn't slow because the future won't cooperate; a method can move at the speed the material allows. One page of seeking costs the plan nothing, and the next step gets its turn.

cells.tense: That shape used to get made here, and the pen stopped before it could.
cells.ask: Place one solid piece of the structure — something that will still hold next month — and then stop.
cells.core: You can organize a mess into a working shape, and somewhere the pen got set down. The thing that needs organizing is still there, and the building wouldn't fall if you came back to it; it could take one piece. The strength to hold a form is yours. It's standing down, not broken. Place one solid piece of the structure — something that will still hold next month — and then stop. Lay it the way a builder sets stone, without deciding what the whole is for. Laying one piece gives your hands the feel of weight again, and that feel is the part that's been missing.
cells.sheetLine: The shape is buildable again once you touch it.

cells.tense: The shape gets made here, and your telling of it leaves you out.
cells.act: apprentice yourself to the material thing
cells.ask: Choose one piece of the structure already in place and spend this week as its apprentice, noticing what it asks of you.
cells.core: You set the shape other people work inside, and if someone asked how the arrangement got made, you'd say it was already like that. The pattern is yours. Whoever keeps the plan doesn't think the plan needs a keeper. The architecture is holding while the author has stepped out of the room. Choose one piece of the structure already in place and spend this week as its apprentice, noticing what it asks of you. That returns you to the start of this line, where you find out what a thing needs by staying near it. What you notice belongs in the structure, and the structure can receive it. Nothing has to change for the attention to have been real. You'll see what your hand did.
